title: fix(objectql)!: an objectExtensions body adds no platform system columns to the object it extends
body:
Fixes #24314

Clause-②: no (narrowing) (the inherit route shipped: an extended object no longer reports or stores a system column its own declaration withholds; owes one `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review before the queue)

The line above is the seat's re-declaration of the claim's provisional line, which named the refusal route. The inherit route shipped, not the refusal. The change still narrows a served set: an extended object whose own declaration withholds system columns no longer reports or stores them. So `no (narrowing)` is still the accurate declaration, and the changeset carries it with its ADR-0087 disposition. One write-door corner is honoured where it used to be refused: an audit-named field that an extension declares, on a target whose plan carries no audit family (`managedBy: 'better-auth'`, `systemFields: false`, `systemFields.audit: false`), is no longer forced read-only. The published contract text already says such targets carry no platform governance (`injected-system-columns.ts` plan rows 1–2, and `applyAuditFieldGovernance`'s doc), so no published accept set widens (record 6252593439, ②).

## What changed

`SchemaRegistry.registerObject` (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`) ran `applySystemFields` on every contributor, an `extend` body included. An extension body carries none of the keys the injected-columns plan reads (`managedBy`, `systemFields`, `tenancy`, `ownership`), so it was planned as an ordinary object. The fold then merged `organization_id`, `created_by` and `updated_by` onto targets whose own declaration withholds them. On a non-`sys_` target it also merged `owner_id` and `owning_business_unit_id`.

Now only a base layer (`own` / `overlay`) is planned. The extended object's system columns are its base layer's plan, in whichever order the layers register. `setDeploymentPlatformGlobalObjects` lost its now-empty `extend` arm.

The fold applies `applyAuditFieldGovernance` (from `@objectstack/metadata-core`) to an extender body when the base layer's plan carries the audit family. So an extension-declared `created_at` stays read-only, as #4447 requires; before this change that protection came from planning the extension body. The case is pinned and ablated (1 of 14 red under the mutation, restored to the HEAD blob). `injected-system-columns.ts` and `packages/platform-objects` are untouched. No error code was added and no column is migrated.

## Measured: M1, booted walled kernel, before the fix

The kernel was `bootStack` with `OrganizationsPlugin`, `OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated`, in-process SQLite. Each target got one text field from a package's `objectExtensions`. Tree `68a090fb97`.

| | registered system columns | physical columns added | member: org list / org by id | member: user list / own user by id |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| extended, before | `organization_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by`, `created_at`, `updated_at` on both | `organization_id`, `created_by`, `updated_by` (+ the extension field); `organization_id` NULL on every row | 200 `[]` / **404** | 200 `[]` / **404** |
| control, no extension | `created_at`, `updated_at` | none | 200 (1 row) / 200 | 200 (2 rows) / 200 |
| extended, after | `created_at`, `updated_at` | the extension field only | 200 (1 row) / 200 | 200 (2 rows) / 200 |

`sys_user` behaves the same way as `sys_organization`. A plain member could not read their own user row by id.

**The same defect, in this repo, on the platform's own extension.** plugin-auth extends `sys_sso_provider` (`managedBy: 'better-auth'`, `tenancy.enabled: false`, `lock: 'full'`) with `oidc_client_secret`. Before the fix, the merged object's `organization_id` was the platform's injected read-only `lookup` to `sys_organization`, which replaced the `text` column the object declares. The object also gained `created_by` and `updated_by` columns and a tenant index. After the fix it is the declared `text` column again, with no `created_by`, `updated_by` or tenant index.

## The route, by the four axes

I measured both routes the card offered.

- **Real business need.** Every in-repo extender of a `lock: 'full'` / better-auth object:
  - plugin-auth's `sys_sso_provider` extension. It is real and load-bearing (the encrypted client secret), and it comes from the owning package.
  - the dogfood fixture `admin-ledger-decision-metadata.dogfood.test.ts`. It extends `sys_user` to layer masking classes, and it is a real exercise of the extension door.
  - the spec probe `stack-unmanaged-install-mode.test.ts`. It never reaches the registry: it is a pure spec parse.

  Outside this repo, cloud's `service-tenant` extends `sys_organization` (cloud#3014). Refusing these extensions would leave the platform's own extension needing an owner exemption, and it would break a named external consumer. Its need was not measured as absent.
- **Long-term soundness / contract-first.** The defect is the plan being computed for the wrong body. It covers every target whose plan withholds a column: `systemFields: false`, `tenancy.enabled: false`, `ownership` other than `user`, an authored `organization_id`, platform-global objects, and better-auth. Refusing extensions of `lock: 'full'` targets covers two of those cases. It leaves the rest open, and it leaves plugin-auth's own extension broken (a same-package extension cannot be refused). The refusal also needs two refusal sites, because an extender can register before the owner. The inherit fix is order-independent and has no exemption.
- **Making AI authoring mistakes harder.** After the fix, an extension cannot change a target's system columns by construction. There is no tolerance branch: the extension body is simply not planned. The extension's own columns on a better-auth table were measured harmless on the walled boot: sign-up, organisation create, invite, accept and set-active all ran with them present, and plugin-auth relies on this.
- **Startup focus.** One guard, no new rule or code, and no narrowing of what a package may register.

Why H1's second premise does not hold: H1 said "managedBy's 'extra columns would collide' covers the extension's own fields". That was measured false. The collision is with the injected names: `organization_id` drives the wall, and the injected definition replaced an authored column. The extension's own fields do not collide.

What stays open: `protection.lock`'s docblock says `no-overlay` is the value for objects whose fields `objectExtensions` may extend, and `full` means "no safe extension point at all". The registry does not enforce that sentence on the extension door (the lock is enforced at the metadata save and delete doors). It is recorded in the report's `open_questions` for the seat, and it is not built here.

## Pins

- `packages/objectql/src/registry-extension-system-columns.test.ts`: six target shapes (better-auth, `systemFields: false`, tenancy disabled, `ownership: 'org'`, an authored `organization_id`, an ordinary object), each in both registration orders. The merged object equals the target's own answer plus exactly the extension's field, with indexes equal. One more case checks that the `extend` contributor carries only its authored fields.
- `packages/plugins/organizations/src/object-extension-managed-target.wall.test.ts`: a booted walled kernel with `sys_organization` and `sys_user` extended.
  - Registered and physical columns: the extension field is present and no withheld column is.
  - An org owner (signed up, not the platform owner) and an invited member each read the organisation by list and by id, and each read their own user row by id.
  - Control: the member gets `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND` on an organisation they do not belong to.

**Pin sweep: the flipped pins.** The `?layers=true` `code` layer is deliberately raw (the read exits govern `effective`, never `code`). For an extended object it equalled the list read only because the extension body smuggled the injected columns in. Three pins compared the raw layer to the governed one by field names:

- `packages/rest/src/meta-object-extension-agreement.test.ts`: `code` now equals the owner's declared fields plus the extension's fields. This pin is load-bearing: the ablation reds it.
- `packages/rest/src/meta-object-overlay-extension-fold.test.ts`: it now compares the authored set (`declaredFieldsOf`), the same way every other comparison in that file does.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/showcase-object-extension-meta-read.dogfood.test.ts`: `code` now equals the showcase declaration plus the extension's fields, and `effective` still equals the list read.

These are test-only edits outside the claim's file list, made under the dispatch's pin-sweep instruction.

## Verification record (head `8316f5b58` with origin/main merged, then two commits to the final head `cb986e382`: the audit-governance fold and a changeset note)

- **Ablation, one behaviour, two runs.** I committed the fix first. The mutation (`if (ownership !== 'extend' || 'ABLATION_24314')`) was written with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, and the objectql build ran with `ablation-dist-preflight` confirming the marker was present.
  - Mutated: the registry unit pin went 13/13 red. The walled pin went 4/5 red (the wall control stayed green). The rest `?layers` pin went red.
  - Restored with `git checkout HEAD -- packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`. Proof of the restore: `git diff HEAD` is empty and the blob hash equals HEAD's. The restored build passed `preflight --absent`, and all pins went green again.
- **Suites:**
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql test`: 441 files, 8305 passed (on `cb986e382`).
  - `@objectstack/rest test`: 295 files, 6049 passed, 326 skipped.
  - `@objectstack/plugin-auth test`: 159 files, 3110 passed, 10 skipped.
  - `@objectstack/organizations test`: 14 files, 166 passed.
  - Dogfood: `showcase-object-extension-meta-read`, `showcase-object-extension-scalar-divergence` and `admin-ledger-decision-metadata`, all 20 passed.
  - `marketplace-install-local-uninstall-meta-reads` (cloud-connection) and `package-uninstall-store-refusal.integration` (runtime) both passed.
- **Typecheck:** objectql, organizations, rest and dogfood all exit 0 after the merge.
- **Gates:** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` (no paths) derived 77 commands. I ran all 77 and every one exited 0. `--ran` reconciles: "77 derived, 77 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN".

## Acceptance notes

- **Consumer pointer, cloud `service-tenant` (cloud#3014).**
  - What it does today: it registers `objectExtensions: [{ extend: 'sys_organization', fields: { summary } }]`.
  - The answer it gets after this change: the extension registers, `summary` is a plain column on `sys_organization`, no `organization_id` is created, and owners and members read their organisation again.
  - Pin constraint: a cloud pin at or past this change needs no edit to stay correct.
  - It no longer has to drop the extension. Whether it should still drop it (its card's option A) is that card's call.
- No existing column is dropped. A database that already has the injected `organization_id` / `created_by` / `updated_by` columns on an extended identity table keeps them as undeclared columns, per the claim's no-migration fence. The engine never serves an undeclared column (#21613). The SQL driver's schema-drift report lists them as orphaned, with an opt-in drop. The upgrade ceremony's plan already drops a present `organization_id` on `sys_organization` and `sys_user` (fate 1).
